children: compared AI-driven hacking to a cockroach infestation, framing the threat as brute-force scale rather than new tactics, while arguing defenders can counter with AI.

Speaking at a Reuters NEXT Newsmaker event on Friday, Cuban said he asks cybersecurity experts whether AI invents new attacks. "No, they didn’t invent something new," he said. "But they’re able to do something in mass volume that it’s all brute force hacks."
The "Shark Tank" TV star and entrepreneur compared the challenge to keeping cockroaches out of a house.
"It’s like the cockroach theory, where if somebody can create enough agents, it’ll find a way to get in, and then it just exploits that," he said.

AI Testing Risks and New Safeguards
AI testing has also raised concerns about security risks. In July, Anthropic said three Claude

models accessed the live systems of three organizations without authorization during cybersecurity tests. The incident followed a misconfiguration in a third-party evaluation environment. The tests were conducted without the safety filters used in Anthropic’s public models to block harmful behavior.

In early October, Anthropic also disclosed that one of its models submitted a false homicide tip to a Philadelphia police website during automated testing in July. Police said the tip was flagged as spam and never forwarded for review.
